authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses Package, PackageMember and Import into a lossless CST, the `sv2` command reports acceptance through its exit status, and the corpus sweep runs 23 rejection cases on every gate. Next increment is the last two PackageBodyElement alternatives — ElementFilterMember and AliasMember — and only then pointing the positive sweep at vendor/corpus.
authored.next_step:
PackageMember and MemberPrefix are implemented, and Package is now reached through them rather than dispatched directly — the seam the last entry flagged is closed. Coverage 12/558. 80 unit tests, 4 snapshots, 23 rejection cases.
WHAT THE GRAMMAR SAID:
  - Import and PackageMember can both open with a VisibilityIndicator. Import's is required, MemberPrefix's is optional, so the indicator alone does not say which production you are in — the keyword after it does. at_import() is that test, and it is the first place one token of lookahead was not enough. Both directions are pinned by a test. A bare `import` with no visibility is neither, and still falls to recovery.
  - MemberPrefix builds its node whether or not a visibility is there. The slot exists in the production either way, and a tree that dropped the node when the slot was empty would make every consumer handle two shapes for one construct.
  - DefinitionElement and UsageElement get no node and no coverage marker. They are alternations over element productions, the matched element already says which alternative was taken, and Package is the only one of DefinitionElement's 28 alternatives implemented.
SNAPSHOTS: all four moved, from that one cause. cargo-insta is NOT installed on this machine, so neither `cargo insta review` nor `accept --snapshot` can run. They were accepted one at a time by promoting each .snap.new individually with its reason recorded, after answering the three questions in the refresh-snapshots skill for each: which change caused it, is the new shape the production's shape, did anything disappear. Every token is byte-identical across all four; only the two wrapper levels and the indentation below them changed. Install cargo-insta if you want the sanctioned command back — it needs network, so it is a deliberate act.
NEXT, in order:
  1. ElementFilterMember, then AliasMember — the last two PackageBodyElement alternatives, one per change. ElementFilterMember needs OwnedExpression, which does not exist; AliasMember needs QualifiedName, which does. Expect AliasMember to be the cheaper of the two and consider taking it first. Each needs its clause read through the navigator, a coverage marker, and rejection cases in the same change.
  2. Only then point tests/corpus at vendor/corpus. Until it is wired the sweep's positive half claims nothing and says so on every run: a negative-only sweep is passed by a parser that rejects everything. Acceptance rests on the 311-file round-trip and the parser tests.
KNOWN GAPS in what exists:
  - Trivia attachment is positional, not owned. The new empty MemberPrefix node did NOT capture the trivia around it — checked against the trivia snapshot — but that is the current behaviour rather than a decided convention, and a graphical edit will care which node owns a comment.
  - parse_for_editor() from .claude/rules/syntax.md does not exist yet.
  - `sv2 parse` has no product on stdout: it is a check, not a dump.
  - Three rejection cases are rejections by absence rather than by rule, each saying so in its header and each naming what removes it: import-annotation-body-is-not-implemented (OwnedAnnotation) and package-member-element-is-not-implemented (PartDefinition).
  - cargo-insta is not installed, so any future snapshot move needs the manual promotion above or a deliberate install.

RESOLVED as far as it can be on one machine. The wikis are pinned by receipt: 1651 atoms in .claude/state/wiki-receipts.json, each with its clause, page, the wiki's region_sha256 to the source PDF span, and a file hash. Drift now fails the gate, and a citation naming a receipt that was never pinned now fails scripts/check_citations.py. NOT resolved: the wikis are not in the repository, because their 1651 atoms carry ~2.3 MB of verbatim OMG specification prose with no licence notice, and this repository is MIT and public. So a fresh clone can verify nothing until it builds its own wikis from the specification PDFs, which are not redistributable either. Revisit only if OMG's licensing changes, or if the wiki builder can be pinned and rerun from locally-held PDFs as part of a bootstrap.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.
